provenance: Abstract-level summaries supplied by the project owner (8 October 2026). Level-by-level tables NOT obtained; no per-level angle may be derived from these entries.

PMID_41047402.summary: In healthy volunteers all thoracic vertebral bodies are kyphotically wedged; upper and middle thoracic discs are kyphotic, lower thoracic discs lordotic; vertebral bodies contribute on average 99.4% of total thoracic kyphosis and discs 0.6%.
constraints: every thoracic vertebral body wedge is kyphotic (sign constraint per level)
upper/middle thoracic disc wedges kyphotic; lower thoracic disc wedges lordotic (sign pattern; transition level not given here)
sum of body wedges ~= total T1-T12 kyphosis; sum of disc wedges ~= 0 (0.6% on average)

PMID_31513104.summary: Standing vertebral tilt: T7 approximately horizontal; T1 the most anteriorly tilted and L1 the most posteriorly tilted.
constraints: T7 endplate tilt ~ 0 deg relative to horizontal in standing (apex region)
T1 has the largest anterior tilt and L1 the largest posterior tilt among T1-L1

consistency_with_committed_data.THORACIC_BODY_DISC_2011_disc_anterior_mi: committed cadaveric disc heights show anterior > posterior from T7/T8 to T11/T12 (lordotic disc wedge), consistent in sign with the lower-thoracic lordotic discs above; upper levels are near equal. Sign check only; cadaveric, mixed sex, no AP depths
consistency_with_committed_data.global_target: Hasegawa male T1-T12 kyphosis 43.7 +/- 9 deg (canonical_spine_reference_pose_p1.json) remains the selected global value

use: Sign/pattern checks for any future per-level thoracic distribution; reject a distribution that violates them.
